passages.title: A wetland beside the highway
passages.text:
For years, people described the low field beside a highway as wasted land. It flooded after heavy rain and was difficult to build on. When engineers proposed filling the field to create a parking area, a biology teacher asked the town to examine what the wetland already did.

Her students observed that water spread across the field after storms and then drained slowly. They also recorded frogs, insects, and birds feeding among the reeds. These observations did not prove that the wetland prevented flooding elsewhere, but they suggested that the field stored some rainwater temporarily and provided habitats for several species.

The town council postponed the parking project and requested a drainage study. Some shop owners were disappointed because they wanted more parking spaces. The teacher acknowledged their concerns and suggested comparing alternatives, such as improving public transport access or using an existing paved lot. She argued that decisions should consider both immediate convenience and less visible environmental services.

By the following year, the field had not become a protected reserve. Nevertheless, the discussion had changed: residents were no longer asking only what could be built there, but also what might be lost if the wetland disappeared.

passages.title: What a lunch survey cannot tell us
passages.text:
A student council surveyed eighty classmates about a proposal to add more plant-based meals to the school canteen. Fifty-two respondents said they would try at least one new dish. Excited by the number, the council announced that most students supported replacing the existing lunch menu entirely.

A mathematics teacher asked the council to reconsider its statement. The survey had asked whether students would try a new dish, not whether they wanted the old menu removed. Moreover, the students who chose to answer might have been more interested in food changes than those who ignored the survey. The results were useful, but they did not justify the council's stronger claim.

The council revised its proposal. Instead of replacing every dish, it suggested offering two new options for a month and gathering feedback about taste, price, and portion size. The canteen manager agreed to discuss a trial, provided the meals could be prepared within the existing budget.

The students learned that a survey is not simply a collection of numbers. The meaning of a result depends on exactly what was asked, who answered, and how the findings are interpreted.

passages.title: A sky worth noticing
passages.text:
Nadia used to hurry home after evening lessons without looking above the rooftops. Then her grandfather invited her to watch a meteor shower from a field outside town. They saw only three bright streaks before clouds covered the sky. Nadia was disappointed, but her grandfather said that watching carefully was not the same as expecting a spectacular result.

Over the next month, Nadia began recording what she could see from her balcony. Some evenings the moon was bright, while on others nearby streetlights seemed to hide all but the strongest stars. She wrote down the weather and time beside each observation. Her notebook slowly became a record of conditions, not a competition to count stars.

One night she noticed that the familiar group of stars appeared lower than it had weeks earlier. She asked her science teacher whether the stars had moved closer to the horizon. The teacher explained that the changing position was mainly related to when Nadia observed them as Earth moved around the Sun. The explanation made her curious about the patterns she had not yet recognized.

Nadia still hoped to see another meteor shower. Yet she now valued the evenings when she noticed something ordinary well enough to ask a better question.

passages.title: When museum labels changed
passages.text:
A local history museum displayed farming tools with labels that identified each object's age and material. Visitors often walked past them quickly. Hoping to make the exhibition more engaging, the museum added short stories about how families had used the tools and invited visitors to compare those accounts with photographs.

After the changes, more visitors stopped at the display. Some staff members immediately credited the new labels. Others pointed out that the museum had also extended its weekend opening hours and introduced free student entry. Without more information, no one could determine how much each change contributed to the increase.

The museum then invited visitors to leave anonymous comments about what had helped them understand the objects. Many appreciated the family stories; several also asked for larger text and translations. The curators responded by testing clearer labels with small groups of students before replacing the entire display.

The project reminded the team that access is not only about getting people through the door. A museum is more useful when visitors can connect what they see to experiences they recognize, question the information presented, and find explanations they can actually read.

questions.prompt: Apa gagasan pokok yang paling tepat?
choices: Setiap lahan basah pasti menghentikan banjir.
Lahan yang tampak tidak berguna mungkin memiliki fungsi yang perlu dinilai sebelum diubah.
Area parkir tidak boleh dibangun di kota mana pun.
questions.explanation: Penulis membahas kebutuhan menilai manfaat tak terlihat sebelum mengubah fungsi lahan.
questions.evidence: what might be lost if the wetland disappeared

questions.prompt: Apa yang diamati siswa setelah hujan deras?
choices: Air menyebar lalu surut secara perlahan
questions.explanation: Hasil observasi menunjukkan air tertahan sementara.
questions.evidence: water spread across the field after storms and then drained slowly

questions.prompt: Apa batas penting dari pengamatan siswa?
choices: Pengamatan belum membuktikan dampak terhadap banjir di wilayah lain
Tidak ada hewan di sekitar lahan
questions.explanation: Teks secara eksplisit membatasi klaim dari hasil observasi.
questions.evidence: These observations did not prove that the wetland prevented flooding elsewhere

questions.prompt: Kata “acknowledged” dalam paragraf ketiga paling dekat dengan …
questions.explanation: Guru mengakui kekhawatiran pemilik toko sebelum menawarkan alternatif.
questions.evidence: The teacher acknowledged their concerns

questions.prompt: Bagaimana diskusi warga berubah?
choices: Dari semata soal pembangunan menjadi juga soal kerugian jika lahan basah hilang
Dari sekolah ke pertandingan sepak bola
questions.explanation: Paragraf terakhir membandingkan pertanyaan dahulu dan sesudah perdebatan.
questions.evidence: residents were no longer asking only what could be built there, but also what might be lost if the wetland disappeared.

questions.prompt: Apa pelajaran utama dari survei tersebut?
choices: Angka survei selalu cukup untuk mengubah kebijakan.
Kesimpulan harus sesuai pertanyaan dan karakteristik responden.
Makanan nabati tidak boleh disajikan di sekolah.
Delapan puluh siswa mewakili seluruh penduduk kota.
questions.explanation: Paragraf akhir menjelaskan pentingnya pertanyaan, responden, dan interpretasi.
questions.evidence: depends on exactly what was asked, who answered, and how the findings are interpreted

questions.prompt: Berapa responden yang bersedia mencoba sedikitnya satu menu baru?
questions.explanation: Bacaan memberi jumlah responden dan jawaban positif.
questions.evidence: Fifty-two respondents said they would try at least one new dish.

questions.prompt: Mengapa klaim dewan siswa terlalu kuat?
choices: Survei menanyakan kemauan mencoba, bukan mengganti seluruh menu.
Tidak ada siswa yang menjawab survei.
questions.explanation: Klaim mengganti keseluruhan menu tidak diukur.
questions.evidence: The survey had asked whether students would try a new dish, not whether they wanted the old menu removed.

questions.prompt: Makna “provided” dalam kalimat manajer kantin adalah …
questions.explanation: Provided di sini memperkenalkan syarat kesediaan mempertimbangkan uji coba.
questions.evidence: provided the meals could be prepared within the existing budget

questions.prompt: Bagaimana sikap guru matematika terhadap hasil survei?
choices: Menganggapnya bermanfaat tetapi tidak mendukung klaim yang berlebihan
Mendukung penghapusan menu lama tanpa syarat
questions.explanation: Guru meminta revisi karena penafsiran melampaui data.
questions.evidence: The results were useful, but they did not justify the council's stronger claim.

questions.prompt: Apa perkembangan utama tokoh Nadia?
choices: Dari ingin tontonan spektakuler menjadi pengamat yang cermat dan ingin bertanya
Dari mengamati langit menjadi takut bintang
Dari menulis catatan menjadi berhenti belajar
Dari rumah ke kota baru setiap minggu
questions.explanation: Nadia belajar menghargai proses pengamatan, bukan banyaknya bintang atau meteor.
questions.evidence: she now valued the evenings when she noticed something ordinary well enough to ask a better question

questions.prompt: Apa yang dicatat Nadia selain hasil pengamatannya?
questions.explanation: Ia mencatat kondisi untuk memahami pola.
questions.evidence: She wrote down the weather and time beside each observation.

questions.prompt: Mengapa catatan kondisi penting untuk pengamatan Nadia?
choices: Karena visibilitas bintang dapat berubah menurut cahaya dan cuaca
Karena semua bintang selalu terlihat sama
questions.explanation: Teks membandingkan bulan terang, lampu jalan, dan kondisi berbeda.
questions.evidence: nearby streetlights seemed to hide all but the strongest stars

questions.prompt: Dalam kalimat terakhir, kata “ordinary” berarti …
questions.explanation: Ordinary berlawanan dengan hasil spektakuler yang sebelumnya diharapkan.
questions.evidence: noticed something ordinary well enough to ask a better question

questions.prompt: Bagaimana nada akhir bacaan?
questions.explanation: Akhir teks menunjukkan refleksi positif atas rasa ingin tahu.
questions.evidence: The explanation made her curious about the patterns she had not yet recognized.

questions.prompt: Apa fokus utama proyek museum?
choices: Membantu pengunjung memahami dan terhubung dengan koleksi
questions.explanation: Perubahan label dilakukan untuk pemahaman dan keterlibatan pengunjung.
questions.evidence: visitors can connect what they see to experiences they recognize

questions.prompt: Perubahan lain apa yang terjadi bersamaan dengan label baru?
choices: Jam akhir pekan diperpanjang dan siswa mendapat tiket gratis
questions.explanation: Dua kebijakan lain membuat dampak label tidak bisa dipisahkan begitu saja.
questions.evidence: extended its weekend opening hours and introduced free student entry

questions.prompt: Kesimpulan paling hati-hati tentang kenaikan pengunjung yang berhenti di pajangan adalah …
choices: Perubahan label mungkin membantu, tetapi faktor lain juga bisa berperan.
Label lama lebih efektif daripada label baru.
questions.explanation: Perbandingan tidak mengendalikan perubahan lain.
questions.evidence: no one could determine how much each change contributed to the increase

questions.prompt: Pada frasa “The curators responded”, “curators” merujuk pada …
questions.explanation: Curators bertanggung jawab mengembangkan label pameran.
questions.evidence: The curators responded by testing clearer labels

questions.prompt: Mengapa teks menggunakan komentar anonim?
choices: Untuk mengumpulkan pengalaman dan kebutuhan pengunjung
Untuk memutuskan benda mana yang harus dijual
questions.explanation: Komentar dipakai untuk melihat apa yang membantu pemahaman dan kebutuhan akses.
questions.evidence: leave anonymous comments about what had helped them understand the objects.
